phases.title: Commit the already-applied prod reference-seed fix + wrapper script

outputs.notes: Ops-verification commit only, no schema change. Verified all three files matched the plan's expected content exactly: scripts/seed-reference-data.ts jsonPath now points at docs/archive/compliance-research/homeschool-requirements-2026-06-27.json (fixed from the missing docs/compliance-research/... path); scripts/seed-reference-prod.ts mirrors scripts/migrate-prod.ts (loads DATABASE_URL_PROD, remaps to DATABASE_URL, execSync's seed-reference-data.ts via npx tsx); package.json's db:seed:reference:prod entry (dotenv -e .env.local -- tsx scripts/seed-reference-prod.ts) was already present in the committed baseline (package.json's only working-tree diff was the routine pre-commit version bump). Reference seed already run and verified against prod 2026-07-16: 66 compliance_rulesets across 7 states (TX/FL/NY/PA/CA/MI/CT), 8 starter badge_definitions — read-only verification, no schema change here. Committed as 4b48c33. IMPORTANT for next worker/orchestrator: `npm run build` fails in this sandbox at static generation of /(shell)/about/page — it calls listChangelogEntries() which needs a live DB connection; TCP connects to the Render Postgres host but the Postgres protocol handshake hangs indefinitely (confirmed via direct postgres.js and raw TCP probes), causing Next's 60s-per-attempt static-export timeout after 3 retries. Confirmed via `git stash` that this reproduces identically with this phase's 3 files stashed out — it is a pre-existing sandbox network/DB-connectivity limitation, NOT caused by this phase's changes, and outside this phase's file scope (features/lib/server/db.ts, app/(shell)/about/page.tsx). npm test passes fully (239 suites, 2110 tests) since tests mock the repository boundary. Later phases whose doneWhen includes `npm run build` should expect this same failure mode in this environment and should not attribute it to their own changes without first checking build fails identically on a clean stash.

phases.title: G1 — Persist Planning Defaults & Records/Compliance settings tabs with an explicit Save button

outputs.notes: Route pattern followed: features/badges/api/router.ts + features/badges/api/routes/settings.ts (most recently added sibling router) — new top-level GET/PUT /api/settings route added to app/api/[...slug]/route.ts's handleRoute() dispatch (new 'settings' slug case, after 'badges'). Reused the existing features/settings/server/repository.ts (getAllHouseholdSettings/setHouseholdSetting against household_settings) unchanged — no duplication. Exact setting keys used: planning.maxLessonsPerDay (number), planning.carryForward ('none'|'next-day'|'next-week'), records.trackingMethod ('days'|'hours'), records.exportFormat ('pdf'|'csv'). Front contract for G7/G8: features/settings/front/services/api.ts exports settingsApi.getSettings() -> ApiResponse<Record<string,unknown>> and settingsApi.updateSettings(patch: Record<string,unknown>) -> ApiResponse<Record<string,unknown>|null> (PUT merges/upserts only the provided keys, returns the full updated map). Both PlanningDefaultsTab.tsx and RecordsComplianceTab.tsx load on mount, track dirty state against last-saved values, and disable the 'Save changes' button until dirty — confirmed via integration tests. No auto-save on change, per plan decision. Found and fixed a test race during TDD: an integration test's initial waitFor assertion (toHaveValue matching the default state, which happened to equal the mocked loaded value) passed before the component's load effect actually finished, so a subsequent userEvent.selectOptions fired on a still-disabled <select> and silently no-op'd. Fixed by asserting `.not.toBeDisabled()` in the waitFor instead of relying on the value coincidentally matching. `npm run build` fails identically to the phase-0 note (static generation of /(shell)/about times out on a DB handshake) — confirmed via `git stash`/`git stash pop` with this phase's files fully stashed out: same 3-retry 60s timeout on /(shell)/about, unrelated to any file in this phase's scope. `npx tsc --noEmit` shows only pre-existing unrelated errors (subjects/messaging/feedback-steward fixtures) — nothing in features/settings/**.

phases.title: G4 — Compliance empty-state copy + info tooltips for ruleset/pathway

outputs.notes: No existing dedicated tooltip component was found in the codebase (grepped for Tooltip/title= across features/**/front/**/*.tsx); used the plan's documented fallback — a plain <span title="..."> wrapper around the lucide-react Info icon (lucide-react's Info component does not accept a `title` prop directly in its LucideProps type, so the title attribute must live on a wrapping element) plus small visible helper-text paragraphs below the ruleset select and pathway input, per ui-style-guide's 'don't invent a new global tooltip component for this alone' guidance. RulesetCard's editing view now branches on rulesets.length === 0: empty case renders a muted explanatory message ('No rulesets available yet for your state...') in place of the <select>; non-empty case keeps the <select> plus a data-testid='ruleset-select-info' info icon and helper text, and the Pathway field always gets a data-testid='pathway-info' info icon and helper text (pathway is free-text and usable even without a ruleset). 'Mark deadline complete' was left untouched per the plan. Build note: `npm run build` reproduces the exact same known sandbox failure documented by phase-0 and phase-g1 (static generation of /(shell)/about times out on a DB handshake after 3x60s retries) — cross-checked via `git stash` (stashing this phase's 2 files + progress.json, running `npm run build` with a 120s bounded timeout, observing the identical `/(shell)/about ... took more than 60 seconds` failure) before `git stash pop` restored the work. `npx tsc` build step did initially catch a real type error introduced by this phase (Info icon does not accept `title` prop) which was fixed by wrapping in <span title=...> before the stash-comparison run — so the build's type-check portion was exercised and passed on this phase's code, only the static-generation phase (unrelated to this phase) fails.

Followed the ui-style-guide collapsible-add-form pattern (§5, same as planner's 'Add lesson' toggle): the header toggle button (data-testid='add-badge-toggle') was renamed from 'Create badge' to 'Add badge' when hidden / 'Cancel' when the form is open, and the form's own submit button keeps the label 'Create badge' (submitLabel prop, unchanged) so the two are no longer text-ambiguous. Added one line of helper text under the 'Add badge' form heading: 'Badges you create here are custom to your household — design your own goals for your kids to work toward.' Fixed a real discoverability gap beyond the label rename: previously the collection.length===0 branch returned early WITHOUT the header/toggle at all, so there was no way to add a badge from the empty state — restructured BadgesPage() to always render the header (with the Add badge toggle) and branch only the body between EmptyBadgeState and the trophy-case grid. Updated the pre-existing 'authors a custom badge via the create form' test to click 'Add badge' instead of 'Create badge' for the toggle, and added two new tests: one confirming the header control is visible/labeled 'Add badge' and reveals the form with helper text, and one confirming it is present even when the collection is empty. `npm run build` reproduces the same known sandbox failure documented by phase-0/g1/g4 (static generation of /(shell)/about times out on a DB handshake after 3x60s retries, unrelated to this phase's 2-file scope) — the build's earlier type-check/lint step completed successfully before that unrelated failure. Committed as 385c6bd.

phases.title: G6 — Verify parent display name works for magic-link users; fix only if a real gap is found

testsRun: npx jest --testPathIgnorePatterns="/node_modules/" -- features/settings/__tests__/integration/SettingsPage.test.tsx features/layout/__tests__/Header.test.tsx features/household/__tests__/api/user-profile.test.ts (3 suites / 36 tests passed)
outputs.notes: NO GAP FOUND — verification only, no functional code change made (working tree left clean, no commit created since nothing changed). Confirming tests already existed pre-phase and were inspected/run, not newly written: SettingsPage.test.tsx's 'Display name — Your profile section' describe block (renders form, pre-fills from session.user.name, saves via householdApi.updateUserProfile + updateSession({name}), shows success/error), Header.test.tsx's 'Header — authenticated' block (greeting uses session.user.name when set, falls back to 'there' — never to email — when absent; email always shown separately in parens), and household/__tests__/api/user-profile.test.ts (PUT /api/household/user-profile persists via updateUserName to the users table). Traced full chain end-to-end: SettingsPage.handleSaveDisplayName -> householdApi.updateUserProfile -> PUT /api/household/user-profile -> updateUserName(userId, name) persists users.name -> updateSession({name}) -> NextAuth jwt callback (features/auth/auth.ts, trigger==='update') sets token.name -> session callback sets session.user.name -> Header.tsx reads session.user.name directly. Session strategy is 'jwt' globally (features/auth/auth.config.ts: session.strategy='jwt', applies to ALL providers) with no provider-specific branching on the name field anywhere in the jwt/session callbacks or resolveTenant — magic-link (Resend), credentials/password, dev-bypass, and OAuth sessions all flow through the identical code path. Conclusion: the display-name flow already works correctly for magic-link sessions exactly as documented in the plan's expected 'no-op verified' outcome — G6 is a no-op verification, not a fix.
